transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

Yes, there's a quick, safe check worth doing first that could save you a call-out. The fan turning, the light coming on and the grill working tell us the cooker is getting power, so the problem looks limited to the oven's heating side. From what you have described, the most likely cause is fan / rear ring element [fan-oven mode]. Set it to 180°C on the fan function for 15 minutes. Is it heating up properly now, or still not?
did that already, its been 20 mins at 180 on fan oven n still stone cold, orange light stays on tho. fan going round fine. what next?
Next: A visibly split/blistered element can be identified by eye (power off). Let me know what you find.
ok isolated it at the cooker switch on the wall n took the back panel off (4 screws). the round element has a blister/split in the coil near the bottom with a black mark on it. is that the problem?

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
Yes, almost certainly: a blistered or split coil with a black burn mark is the classic sign of a failed fan oven element. That fits everything you've described, with the fan turning, the light on and the grill working, but no heat at all in fan mode. The checks point to the fan oven element. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on the frame around the oven door opening.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its an Indesit IFW 6330 IX, read it off the rating plate on the door frame. is that enough to get the right element?

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
Mostly, yes. The model number from the rating plate is the main thing you need. The checks point to the fan oven element.
